scope: Exploratory tuning on the previously seen 24 evaluation tasks x 3 seeds. Not fresh generalization. Independent agents only.
question: Does client-side budget forcing (continue the same token sequence after a forced end of thinking) beat the scribe commit (new thinking-off request with own notes pasted) at the same 8192-token budget and prompt wording?
method: K=4 independent forced_explicit agents per case (index_explicit prompt; thinking up to 7168 tokens via raw completions on the server chat template; if cut without closing thinking, append "\n</think>\n" and continue the same sequence with the remaining budget). Compare with the 4 scribe_explicit agents per case of nemotron72-known-swarm-v1 (same prompt, 7936 + 256). Case solved if any agent plan passes the original exact verifier; all agents run to completion. Trigger equals the scribe trigger (no parsed plan, finish=length, own tokens): if thinking was never closed the end is forced; if thinking closed but the answer was cut, the same sequence simply continues.
seeds: agent seed = 1000*case_seed + 100 + agent_index; disjoint from seeds 1,2,3 and from the swarm run (offset 0)

limits.deadline_note: No wall-clock quality limit. 120 s without any streamed byte = hung server (infrastructure fault). Deadlines are catastrophe stops only; run_benchmark labels them controller_180_second_deadline (legacy label).
limits.transport_wall_limit_seconds_note: 1800 s per call (catastrophe only); the 2400 s agent deadline is reached first in the worst case.

scheduling.placement: agent j of case c runs on replica (c+j)%4; per-replica FIFO queues in case order

primary_outcome: per-agent success rate forced_explicit vs scribe_explicit (swarm v1 odd agents) and solved cases with 4 agents each; secondary: tokens per solved case, forced-trigger and conversion rates
stop_policy: Controller/transport/malformed-trace/process faults or source change stop new admissions; in-flight agents finish.
